questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
I've only been to Italy once in my life and that was a very long time ago. I've always admired the Italian culture from afar and have always wanted to spend more time in the country. Thus, being able to spend a semester in Milan was ideal for me, also considering the fact that I've heard so many great things about it from friends who've gone there previously.

It was also important to me that I had heard that the academic level - at least as far as for Erasmus students are concerned - was quite limited compared to the level at my home university. As checked out above, the most important thing for me was in no way the academic outcome - it was the experience to live abroad and have a good time.

It wasn't an absolute deal breaker for me, but the possibility to receive the Erasmus grant was also one of the pros by choosing a destination within Europa, and within Europe there was little doubt that Milan would be my preferred destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think the communication from the host university was fine. I personally didn't have any issues in that regard.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received information by email about how to register as arrived, how to sign up for courses etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
My roommate and I were quite late on the market, but it didn't take us too long to find a place and we lived pretty centrally.
However, we did pay quite a lot in rent, so I would recommend searching for options a long time before you go there.
We used the website
spotahome.com
which worked very well.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Look for a place a long time before you go to your destination.

Also, I think it is well worth the extra rent to pick an apartment that seems like a place you'd like to be and that also is located quite centrally.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I only looked off campus, and I think (despite the fact that we were late on the market) that the options were good.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to apply for acceptance at the host university which was pretty easy and a formality. Then I was requested to forward some documentation (passport, insurance etc.).

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could always write to the person of contact at the host university and I think he was fine at responding.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. I got all the courses I wanted and I was able to change them during the semester if needed.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just follow the instruction sent to you by email, and if you are in any doubt, contact the person of contact at the host university.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
My expectation and hope was that the academic programme would be very easy which turned out to be exactly the case.

So I was very satisfied.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The content of some of the classes could at times be challenging but the exams were easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was a lot less student interactive and it was more in a lecture format-

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- Competition Law and Economics
- European Monetary and Economic Law
- Law and Policies of Social Rights Protection in Europe
- Collective Redress and Sustainability
- Comparative Labour Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Competition Law and Economics: very interesting course and the teacher is knowledgable

European Monetary and Economic Law: interesting content and the exam is easy (15 minutes presentation, 2 people, topic of your own choosing)

Law and Policies of Social Rights Protection in Europe: easy exam, just a written paper and a very short "defense" of the paper.

Collective Redress and Sustainability: the teacher is a bit special, however, the exam is alright and you can make the assignment after you go home.

Comparative Labour Law: very entertaining teacher.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't use them, so I have no opinion on this one.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: No idea.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
- Going to the San Siro to watch football.
- Exploring the culture of the city (the Duomo, the museums etc.)
- Eating and drinking.
- Finding local spots.
- Going on trips around Italy (I would especially recommend going to Napoli).

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: The same as the above.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It took a few weeks (mainly because I didn't have school for the first few weeks), but it came quite quickly after that.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
We were many Danes so I spend most time with them.

Some of my friends went to activities (salsa dancing, cooking courses etc.) and had success with that.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: In Milan they are very bad pedestrians.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The food and the wine and the fact that the locals actually wanted to speak Italian if you tried.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) really don't spend too much time at school - just enjoy.
2) when making a decision to do or not do something, remember that this is (probably) a once in a lifetime opportunity.
3) find a place to stay that you actually like being at.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not anything else than already mentioned.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Having fun with lovely people and just being able to enjoy life without having to think about school or work.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The kitchen in our apartment wasn't the best.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
